method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)' (first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027), 23 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0. eviQ also states that its content should not be hosted on external sites, and that commercial entities must contact eviQ to seek permission (https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright). Adaptations must cite the eviQ ID, version and URL. (read at https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright (Disclaimer and copyright page)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Conference on Infections in Leukaemia (ECIL-6; EBMT, EORTC, ICHS, ELN), Cesaro S (chair), Dalianis T, Hanssen Rinaldo C, Koskenvuo M, Einsele H, Hirsch HH 'ECIL 6 - Guidelines for the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of BK Polyomavirus Associated Hemorrhagic Cystitis in Stem Cell Transplant Patients (final slide set)' (final slide set 8 December 2015 (published as J Antimicrob Chemother 2018;73:12-21)), 6 claims; LICENCE: No licence or reuse terms stated in the slide set or on ecil-leukaemia.com (treated as all rights reserved) (read at the slide set itself and https://www.ecil-leukaemia.com/en/resources/resources-ecil). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 keeps every edition 1.0 claim and anchor (S1, eviQ 1297) unchanged and adds S2, the ECIL-6 guideline on BK polyomavirus haemorrhagic cystitis after stem-cell transplant, for diagnosis, prophylaxis and treatment of the late viral form. The journal version (JAC 2018) and the 2024 AIEOP paediatric consensus were not openly readable (paywall or bot challenge); ECIL's own final slide set was used. Its summary tables extracted as interleaved columns; only rows whose text runs cleanly are anchored.

claims.claim: **Cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide are the commonest cause.** The liver converts both to acrolein, which the kidneys excrete; the longer acrolein sits against the bladder lining, the more it injures the urothelium.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **About 20–25% of patients develop it in the weeks or months after cyclophosphamide**, and the risk climbs with larger single and cumulative doses.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other causes include** busulfan, cabazitaxel, antithymocyte globulin, intravesical therapy, pelvic radiotherapy, and infection (BK virus, adenovirus, CMV) in immunosuppressed allogeneic transplant recipients.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Roughly 30% of blood and marrow transplant patients get HC**, mostly after allogeneic transplant. Early-onset HC (within 72 hours of finishing conditioning) is prevented with mesna and hyperhydration; late-onset HC (from about day +30) is usually a viral reactivation.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Low-dose oral cyclophosphamide still carries risk:** take the dose as early in the day as possible so less active metabolite stays in the bladder overnight, drink well, empty the bladder often, and act on symptoms promptly.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Radiation-induced HC can appear years later:** onset averages about 31.8 months after pelvic radiotherapy, with a range from 6 months to beyond 10 years.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Symptoms:** blood in the urine (microscopic to visible, with or without clots), painful, frequent or urgent voiding, incontinence, night-time voiding and suprapubic or vague abdominal pain. Anyone with symptoms should be seen by a medical officer.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Work-up:** examine the lower abdomen and do a post-void bladder scan, take a medication history, send urinalysis and culture to rule out infection, arrange cystoscopy and/or cytology to rule out malignancy, and check a full blood count.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **CTCAE grading:** grade 3 is visible haematuria needing transfusion, IV medicines or admission; grade 4 has life-threatening consequences and needs urgent invasive intervention.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prevention aims to dilute acrolein and shorten its contact with the bladder:** IV or oral hydration or hyperhydration, mesna, voiding often and at the first urge (sitting or standing rather than lying down), frusemide if urine production falls below 100 mL/m²/hr, and urine output kept above 100 mL/hr.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No clear guidance exists for preventing radiation-induced HC.**
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mesna binds acrolein**, is cleared quickly by the kidneys and leaves the anticancer action of both drugs intact. Routes: by mouth or IV, as a bolus or an infusion.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Mesna has to be in the bladder already when the chemotherapy is given.** Keep it going for the whole chemotherapy and for 12 to 24 hours afterwards, until the toxic metabolites have fallen away.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dosing is not standardised, and the evidence is old:** ASCO last updated its mesna-with-ifosfamide advice in 2008, and no randomised trials had appeared since its 2002 version. In 2013 the eviQ Haematology Reference Committee chose to match mesna to ifosfamide at 1:1 in its protocols; other doses may be reasonable.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ifosfamide under 2.5 g/m²/day as a short infusion:** the day's IV mesna totals 60% of the ifosfamide dose, split into three boluses: 15 minutes before each ifosfamide dose, then at 4 hours and at 8 hours after it.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ifosfamide under 2.5 g/m²/day by continuous infusion:** an IV mesna bolus worth 20% of the daily ifosfamide dose alongside the ifosfamide, then a mesna infusion worth 40% running during the ifosfamide and for 12 to 24 hours after it ends.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ifosfamide above 2.5 g/m²/day:** the evidence is too thin to set a mesna dose; because ifosfamide lingers longer at high doses, mesna may need to be given more often and for longer.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral mesna is dosed at double the IV dose and should not be used for the first dose.** Give IV mesna 20% of the daily ifosfamide dose with the ifosfamide, then oral mesna 40% at 2 and 6 hours after the infusion finishes, so total mesna equals 100% of the ifosfamide. Oral plus IV protects about as well as IV alone. If the patient vomits within 2 hours of an oral dose, repeat it or switch to IV.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **High-dose cyclophosphamide (50 mg/kg or 2 g/m²) for stem-cell transplant:** hyperhydration alone or with mesna. Hyperhydrate with at least 3 L/m² over 24 hours; if mesna is added, give it IV at 1.0–1.5 times the daily cyclophosphamide dose.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treatment is individual and scaled to severity; no evidence-based standard exists.** Mild HC usually passes with fluids, bladder anticholinergics and analgesia; moderate to severe HC may need more active measures.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Rule out bacterial, fungal, viral and parasitic infection before treating**, and treat any infection found. Late viral HC needs treatment of the virus as well as the symptoms.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Options:** stop the offending drug, hyperhydrate, give analgesia and antispasmodics, irrigate clots by hand or with continuous bladder irrigation, and transfuse red cells and platelets as needed. For severe or refractory HC, cystoscopic clot evacuation, a suprapubic catheter, hyperbaric oxygen or intravesical agents have been reported.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Teach patients at risk** to keep well hydrated, avoid alcohol and caffeine, void regularly and as soon as they feel the urge, take oral cyclophosphamide in the morning and oral mesna on schedule, and report blood in the urine, urgency or frequency, painful voiding, vague abdominal pain or waking often at night to pass urine.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '1297 Haemorrhagic cystitis (eviQ ID 1297, version 6)', first approved 5 March 2012; last reviewed 4 October 2023; review due 30 June 2027, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1297, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diagnosis needs all three:** symptoms and signs of cystitis, haematuria of grade II or above, and BK virus replication (urine viral load above 7 log10 copies/mL). A negative blood viral load does not exclude it.
claims.locator: European Conference on Infections in Leukaemia (ECIL-6; EBMT, EORTC, ICHS, ELN), Cesaro S (chair), Dalianis T, Hanssen Rinaldo C, Koskenvuo M, Einsele H, Hirsch HH, 'ECIL 6 - Guidelines for the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of BK Polyomavirus Associated Hemorrhagic Cystitis in Stem Cell Transplant Patients (final slide set)', final slide set 8 December 2015 (published as J Antimicrob Chemother 2018;73:12-21), https://www.ecil-leukaemia.com/images/resources/2015/3_ECIL6-BK-virus-08-12-2015-Cesaro-S-et-al.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Haematuria grades (ECIL):** II visible blood; III visible blood with clots; IV clots with a rising creatinine or cystatin C, reflecting kidney or bladder dysfunction.
claims.locator: European Conference on Infections in Leukaemia (ECIL-6; EBMT, EORTC, ICHS, ELN), Cesaro S (chair), Dalianis T, Hanssen Rinaldo C, Koskenvuo M, Einsele H, Hirsch HH, 'ECIL 6 - Guidelines for the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of BK Polyomavirus Associated Hemorrhagic Cystitis in Stem Cell Transplant Patients (final slide set)', final slide set 8 December 2015 (published as J Antimicrob Chemother 2018;73:12-21), https://www.ecil-leukaemia.com/images/resources/2015/3_ECIL6-BK-virus-08-12-2015-Cesaro-S-et-al.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Look for, and treat where possible, other contributors:** bacterial, fungal, other viral (JC virus, CMV, adenovirus, HSV) or parasitic infection; urotoxic injury (onset within 1–2 weeks of conditioning with cyclophosphamide, busulfan or TBI, or inadequate diuresis or mesna); low platelets, bleeding disorders or GVHD; urothelial or other cancer; and catheters, stents or ureteric stenosis.
claims.locator: European Conference on Infections in Leukaemia (ECIL-6; EBMT, EORTC, ICHS, ELN), Cesaro S (chair), Dalianis T, Hanssen Rinaldo C, Koskenvuo M, Einsele H, Hirsch HH, 'ECIL 6 - Guidelines for the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of BK Polyomavirus Associated Hemorrhagic Cystitis in Stem Cell Transplant Patients (final slide set)', final slide set 8 December 2015 (published as J Antimicrob Chemother 2018;73:12-21), https://www.ecil-leukaemia.com/images/resources/2015/3_ECIL6-BK-virus-08-12-2015-Cesaro-S-et-al.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Do not screen well transplant recipients for BK virus in urine or blood outside studies** (D II): BK is found in more than 80% after allogeneic transplant, and a qualitative urine PCR is not informative.
claims.locator: European Conference on Infections in Leukaemia (ECIL-6; EBMT, EORTC, ICHS, ELN), Cesaro S (chair), Dalianis T, Hanssen Rinaldo C, Koskenvuo M, Einsele H, Hirsch HH, 'ECIL 6 - Guidelines for the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of BK Polyomavirus Associated Hemorrhagic Cystitis in Stem Cell Transplant Patients (final slide set)', final slide set 8 December 2015 (published as J Antimicrob Chemother 2018;73:12-21), https://www.ecil-leukaemia.com/images/resources/2015/3_ECIL6-BK-virus-08-12-2015-Cesaro-S-et-al.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Prophylaxis:** hyperhydration during conditioning is supported (B II) because it counters the urotoxic effect of cyclophosphamide or busulfan; in a randomised trial, 2 mL/kg/h with mesna and 4 mL/kg/h with forced diuresis gave similar HC rates (26.8% vs 23.7%). Bladder irrigation is graded C II (invasive, uncomfortable). **Ciprofloxacin is not recommended** (D II): little effect on the virus and none on HC.
claims.locator: European Conference on Infections in Leukaemia (ECIL-6; EBMT, EORTC, ICHS, ELN), Cesaro S (chair), Dalianis T, Hanssen Rinaldo C, Koskenvuo M, Einsele H, Hirsch HH, 'ECIL 6 - Guidelines for the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of BK Polyomavirus Associated Hemorrhagic Cystitis in Stem Cell Transplant Patients (final slide set)', final slide set 8 December 2015 (published as J Antimicrob Chemother 2018;73:12-21), https://www.ecil-leukaemia.com/images/resources/2015/3_ECIL6-BK-virus-08-12-2015-Cesaro-S-et-al.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Treatment:** best supportive care (analgesia, hydration, and platelet transfusion at a higher threshold) is graded A III; hyperbaric oxygen (where available) and fibrin glue by cystoscopy are C III. **IV cidofovir is graded C II with no set dose:** studies used 3–5 mg/kg when probenecid is given, or 0.5–1.5 mg/kg when it is not. Intravesical cidofovir has too little experience for a recommendation.
claims.locator: European Conference on Infections in Leukaemia (ECIL-6; EBMT, EORTC, ICHS, ELN), Cesaro S (chair), Dalianis T, Hanssen Rinaldo C, Koskenvuo M, Einsele H, Hirsch HH, 'ECIL 6 - Guidelines for the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of BK Polyomavirus Associated Hemorrhagic Cystitis in Stem Cell Transplant Patients (final slide set)', final slide set 8 December 2015 (published as J Antimicrob Chemother 2018;73:12-21), https://www.ecil-leukaemia.com/images/resources/2015/3_ECIL6-BK-virus-08-12-2015-Cesaro-S-et-al.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24
